newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Funds short to demobilise 73,000 Angolan soldiers.
newsitem.headline: Funds short to demobilise 73,000 Angolan soldiers.

text.p: The demobilisation of 73,000 UNITA and government soldiers in Angola will be in jeopardy at the end of this month unless funds are forthcoming, an aid agency said on Tuesday.

The International Organisation for Migration (IOM), which launched an appeal to Western donors last month, has received $3.6 million from Britain, Denmark, Italy, Portugal and the U.N. Development Programme, according to a spokeswoman.
"This is enough to continue through the end of June but we will have to reevaluate the financial situation in mid-June so we know whether we can proceed or stop," she told a news briefing.

The Geneva-based IOM needs $12.4 million to complete its demobilisation of 43,000 former rebels of the National Union for the Total Independence of Angola (UNITA). Under the six-month programme begun in mid-April, they are to be sent home with some 116,000 dependents.
In a second phase expected to cost $10 million, some 30,000 government soldiers and 112,000 dependents are to be sent home.

"UNITA is the focus for the moment. Once demobilisation of UNITA is completed, we will move on to the Angola regular army," Eugenio Ambrosi, head of IOM's humanitarian programmes bureau for Africa, told Reuters.
"We will continue operations for as long as we have funds."
